The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3bf9877aaa27427d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: For every fixed nonempty finite alphabet, finite monoid M, and finite represen- tation space V , all parameters in the two outer splits and the five aligned stages can be chosen to satisfy their stated hypotheses. More precisely, the stencils are nonempty, have more than Ci copies of each required kind, and satisfy #{(p, p′ ) ∈ P2 i : p ̸= p′ , AΓi i (t + p − p′ , q)} ≤ Ci (0 ≤ i ≤ 4) on every complete episode. Write Ni = |Pi|. In order, these bounds concern first-clock or prediction failure, inner-search instability, second-clock failure, a right-margin marker, and end-search instability. The constants can be taken to be C0 = K + ccl log(2m1), (7.1) C1 = 10|Z|N4 0 (2R1 + 3), (7.2) C2 = N4 0 N4 1 ccl log(2m2), (7.3) C3 = 10|Z|(2R2 + 3) Y j<3 N4 j , (7.4) C4 = 10(2wE + 3) Y j<4 N4 j . (7.5) Here K = |M||V |2+1, m1, m2 are the respective full tag alphabet sizes, and ccl is the absolute constant of Lemma 3.1; logarithms are natural. Also, diam Pi < wE for i < 4. All measurements, trials, and inspections have the chronological and reading-side access required in Lemmas 5.1, 5.2, and 6.4. Every bounded control, including every control at a false candidate origin, lies inside the true first episode. The same choices satisfy the end margins of Section 4.
